drhp.business: Emkay Global Financial Services, established in 1995, operates an integrated platform spanning Institutional Equities, Investment Banking, Wealth Management, and Asset Management. The company serves over 40,200 clients—including foreign institutional investors, domestic mutual funds, banks, HNIs, and corporates—with research coverage of nearly 240 stocks across 20+ sectors. Its offerings combine a technology-first trading ecosystem with research-led investment intelligence and end-to-end financial solutions under one roof.
drhp.expansion: During FY2025-26, the Company issued 95,00,000 convertible warrants on a preferential basis, with allotments made to promoters and a non-promoter entity. Out of the total consideration, 25% was received at allotment, and the remaining 75% is payable upon conversion into equity shares. Subsequently, 5,56,600 equity shares were allotted upon conversion of warrants during the year. The Company also seeks shareholder approval to increase borrowing limits and create charges on assets to secure additional debt facilities for business purposes.

litigation.note: No material litigation disclosed; no proceedings initiated or pending against the Group for holding Benami property, and the Group is not a declared willful defaulter.

drhp.one_liner: Emkay Global is a research-led, integrated financial services platform built over three decades, delivering capital markets, wealth management, and asset management solutions to institutional and HNI clients across India and international markets.

risks.note: As a SEBI-regulated financial services entity, the Company must continuously adhere to evolving listing, governance, and disclosure regulations. Non-compliance could lead to penalties, reputational damage, or restrictions on business operations.

The preferential allotment of convertible warrants to promoter-group entities (Mr. Krishna Kumar Karwa, Mr. Prakash Kacholia) and a single non-promoter entity (Antique Securities Private Limited) indicates concentrated ownership and decision-making influence, which could affect minority shareholder interests and governance dynamics.

While the statutory auditor provided an unmodified opinion on internal financial controls as of 31st March 2026, the Company acknowledges the need for regular audits and periodic reviews to ensure controls remain effective and are continuously strengthened, implying inherent operational complexity and control reliance.
risks.risk: Internal financial control and operational risk

risks.note: The issuance of 95,00,000 convertible warrants and subsequent equity shares upon conversion can lead to significant equity dilution for existing shareholders, potentially impacting earnings per share and voting rights if conversion occurs at prices below intrinsic value.

The ongoing exercise of stock options under ESOP Plans 2007 and 2018 (2,65,439 shares issued during the year) creates a steady dilution stream and compensation cost, which may affect reported profitability and shareholder returns over time.

The Board has approved an increase in the overall borrowing limit from ₹500 crore to ₹1,000 crore to meet increased financial requirements, particularly for working capital needs. The Company believes its credit rating and strong brand equity enable it to borrow at competitive rates.
